utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, ladies and gentlemen; good morning, interpreters, I can see that you are there; good morning, sound engineers, counsel for the Prosecution, for the Defence, General Krstic; and also good morning to the witness and his interpreter. We shall now resume our case, the Krstic case. For the record, we are all here, the same, except for Judge Wald, who, for urgent and pressing matters, could not join us. Under Rule 15 bis, paragraph (A), the two Judges, Judge Riad and I, believe that the interests of justice, that is, a fair and expedient process, requires that we continue hearing this case. During the absence of Judge Wald, and she will be absent for three days, we have decided to continue hearing the case, and we shall do so by hearing the evidence that was begun yesterday by the witness who is already in the witness box. Mr. McCloskey, it is now up to you. I should like to remind the witness and his interpreter that you are both under oath, and you will now continue to give your testimony. Mr. McCloskey, it is now really time for you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. McCloskey: [Cont'd]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness F, I believe we left off yesterday where you had described the bodies you'd seen and photographed, and you were describing them on the pictures. Now, let me ask you, how close were you able to get to those bodies and view them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 20 to 25 metres. I was on a slope, on an incline, so I didn't see straight ahead. I looked downwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to make out the kinds of clothes that the people were wearing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. McCloskey. The French booth did not hear your question. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to make out the different kinds of clothing that the people were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could. The victims had all civilian clothes; some of them had blue jeans, pullovers, coats. But there were no persons with military clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you make out the sexes of the victims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all men between the ages of approximately 15 to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: -- 45, I believe the witness said. The interpreter is not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you state that again? There was a little bit of an interpretation problem. They didn't make out your last answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all men, in the age group 15 to 45.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you able to see any injury on any of these victims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some of them had bloodstains on their backs and at the back of their heads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do after seeing these victims and photographing them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I climbed back up and I joined my colleague who was standing on guard there. I looked at him. I was in shock. And we immediately returned to the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about what time was that, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around noon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go back outside the compound any time that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: After returning to the compound, I returned, I had a cup of coffee, and then I went back outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was going on outside the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: People were still being deported, taken to buses, just like the first day, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you discussed this briefly, but can you tell us what the senior VRS officers you saw there -- out there that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: High-ranking officers, they were all present again. Some of them were just standing and looking whether things were going according to plan, and for the rest, they didn't do much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you name the officers whose names you now know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person present in the courtroom was there, and some others, some people who just were walking around, not so many, and that was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was also present, indeed, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me. He said they were standing and looking. He didn't say looking at what and standing where. Can I just ask?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those officers were in the vicinity, standing near the vicinity of the main compound, near the interrogation house, and they were just watching whether everything was going to plan, and some of them also went towards the direction of Srebrenica, the officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Near the interrogation house or near the bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next to the interrogation house is where the officers were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did it take until all of the Muslims were transported from the area outside the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Till about dusk, 6.00 or 7.00 in the evening, since it was summertime. I would like to repeat that I don't remember the times, I didn't -- when you live through such days, you don't watch the time, you don't look at your watch. One is a bit unstable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anything happen to the belongings that were in front of the White House after everyone was transported out of the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: All around the compound, there were many personal belongings belonging to those Muslim civilians, mainly next to this White House, the interrogation house. The belongings of all those men were heaped up, the men who had been separated. Most of those belongings were just put on one big heap and then were set afire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you able to photograph this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could show the witness Exhibit 62.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph as a photograph you took?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately when was this taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the end of the evening, when dusk broke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that the same day that the Muslims were finally all transported out of the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you able to see who lit this pile of belongings on fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Negative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could it have been Dutch soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the soldiers you saw in black that you've described earlier, did you ever get close enough to them to be able to identify if they had any emblems on insignias on them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, I was close to them, but I couldn't see any emblems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to make out any emblems or insignia on any of the soldiers that you were close enough to see during those two days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The infantry units only had little strips of fabric on their shoulders, just to show that they were belonging together, and of course the police cars had the letters "Police" written on them. And that was all the emblems I could see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you stay in Potocari for about another week, and then -- until you were finally shipped out with the rest of your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. Now, Witness F, the time has come for you to answer the questions which Mr. Petrusic, as I see, will ask you. He is one of the counsel for the defence of General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, my learned friends. Cross-examined by Mr. Petrusic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness F. In the beginning of your testimony, and today, you referred to units dressed in black uniforms. Did these units have their own command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And independently of units wearing camouflage uniforms of somewhat poorer quality, operated on their own, operated independently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were independent of the black units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. My question is they operated independently of other units, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They didn't do any business with other infantry units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those other infantry units had their own command, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They mainly consisted of NCOs who went along with them, along the lines, and the people in black had their own commanders. So they were separate from each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These units, just for the sake of identification, I will call them the same way you did, that is, poorer dressed units, wearing uniforms of worse quality, engaged in combat with the Muslim units, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us where precisely was this combat in relation to Bratunac-Srebrenica road? Where was fighting taking place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could have a map, I could show you, just to clear things up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just a moment while we show the witness the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. Perhaps it would even be better if -- Mr. Dubuisson is suggesting to use Exhibit 2, and then the witness perhaps could show it on that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Dubuisson will help us now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I make a suggestion, please? Perhaps this will, after all, be a better solution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think you are right, Mr. Petrusic, and I think we should remove the big map, if it is not necessary. If the small map is put on the ELMO, then we can all see it. And perhaps we shall not need the big map, Mr. Dubuisson, perhaps it could be removed. I think that it blocks the view for our interpreters, and they do need to have at least visual communication with Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should also like to ask Mr. Petrusic the number of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, for the record, Exhibit 5A of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I think it is better now, because otherwise we would have to go into a closed session because if the witness had to move about, then it would be difficult to provide the protection measures. Yes, Mr. Petrusic, I think now it will be all right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, when I was on my location, looking towards Bratunac, OP Papa, to the eastern side there were a couple of Muslim fighters, so that is that side [indicates]; to the north we heard sounds, heavy engine sounds, heavy vehicles. It later turned out to be a Russian T-55 tank. They came from the direction -- they came from the western direction. The Muslim fighters fired light mortar from the east towards north, and this fire was answered by Serb machine-gun fire, not tank fire. And their position was such -- my position was such that I saw the shells coming in, I had to crouch behind my sandbag from time to time, because also our position was a bit harmed by this. In the days before the fall of the enclave, there were -- for a couple of days, there was heavy artillery fire to be heard around Srebrenica, and it all came from the north into Srebrenica. A couple of times we had to hide in our bunkers, and in the vicinity of Potocari, here [indicates] in the mountains, there was quite some fire. It was heavy machine-gun fire and mortar shellings. From this direction [indicates], here were Serb positions, there was heavy fire with cannon fire. MT-12 was the type of those cannons, and that went on for a couple of days. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, I'm sorry to cut in, but perhaps we need to have a synthesis of what the witness said, because we are receiving the interpretation "from here to here," but we do not know where he was. Could you give us the coordinate points? Where is Bratunac? Where is Srebrenica? And where was the witness? I think it will be a synthesis, but this is merely a suggestion, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely that is what I wanted to ask about the road between Bratunac and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where exactly did the fighting between Serb and Muslim forces take place? If I may be allowed to continue. The witness, when pointing, because we have those figures on the map, perhaps he will keep the pointer on the figure, or rather on the box, on the square, that he's showing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: My position was in map square 91, this square here [indicates], at the top of this square. I was looking towards map square 64, 65, the square under 65, 90, and 63. The Muslim fighters were all in the map square here [indicates], under this, so that's 59, and they fired from 59 to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last number? Could the witness please repeat the last number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Square 59 is where the Muslim fighters fired their mortars, towards square 64, this general direction [indicates], and this fire was answered with machine-gun fire, and from time to time cannon shots. My position was such that I saw the shells come in and land in this location [indicates]. Sometimes I had to hide behind my position because of the detonations and the shells. In the days before that, before the enclave fell, there was heavy firing from square 64 -- or, I correct myself, 65, up till 83, up to and including 83. Along this line [indicates], there was heavy artillery mortar fire, and the fire was so heavy that the compound was shaking in this vicinity. Around the compound Potocari, I will mark this with a circle here, there were quite some fights taking place in the woods here [indicates]. From the direction of Budak here, square 63, we heard heavy engine sounds. It later turned out to be a tank, T-55, a Russian T-55 tank. It turned on the way to Srebrenica, and later on it entered Srebrenica. Behind the tank there was an armoured vehicle with an anti-aircraft -- which was used for shooting at houses, and of course there were many infantry units with them. The Muslim fighters which were here already were seen to be running back and forth while they were fired at, looking for new positions in the field. In 63, there were also quite some Muslim fighters. Apparently, they tried to resist against advancing Serb military, in square 63 to 66. I could see all of this, I observed it from my position, my location on the compound, in map square 90/91.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. My colleague has pointed out to me that it's not clear who had the anti-aircraft gun, and perhaps that's an important factor for this discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I think that there have been quite a few problems with interpretation here. I believe that the French interpretation has more or less followed, but while Mr. McCloskey was speaking, they were still interpreting the words of the witness. We should try to figure out exactly where the anti-aircraft gun was positioned, I believe that that was the question. After the witness has answered to that question, I will then ask Mr. Petrusic to ask specific questions because the witness has already covered quite a few facts. But let me ask the witness the following question: If we look at the map, if we look at the circle on the map, I think that Bratunac is in the north-westerly direction, whereas Srebrenica is situated towards south. Is that the case, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you therefore be more specific and tell us the exact position of the AA gun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This anti-aircraft gun was placed on a vehicle. I'm not familiar with the kind of vehicle, but the anti-aircraft gun was a ZSU-23.2 [Interpreter's Note: "ZSU-23.2" I believe the witness said] it came from the direction of OP Papa. It was the direction of the compound Potocari, towards the direction of Srebrenica. It halted at the edge of a wood, approximately at a distance of three kilometers -- no, I correct myself -- two kilometres from the compound. They were firing at the positions in the eastern direction, in map square 92, where the Muslim fighters were at that moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, could you now ask your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. My first question was also quite specific, but the witness elaborated on it. I will continue asking very specific questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. But both of you, both you, Mr. Petrusic, and counsel for the Prosecution, can always ask the witness -- can always remind the witness to give specific answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bearing that in mind, therefore, could you tell us the time of day when this conflict between Serbian and Bosnian forces occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were already busy quite early in the morning on that day, and the nearer the Serbs advanced, the fights became heavier. And during the previous days, of course, there were also -- we heard some fights --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Could you now tell us what date it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're mainly talking about the first day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you perhaps refer us to a specific event which took place on a date which you are sure about, to put it somehow in context? And then in respect of that date, if you can please tell us the exact date of this particular event, which is now interesting for us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those -- around the days of the 10th and the 11th, until the Serbs had entered the enclave, then there was hardly any fighting anymore. But I can't very well remember the dates. We just lived from day to day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, Witness F, you testified about a police transporter or personnel carrier that arrived in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the blue vehicle?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It had also arrived, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You refer to it as a police personnel carrier.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That vehicle was a blue vehicle. It was very distinctive between all that green materiel. It was an armoured vehicle, on wheels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any police forces in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the troops had all entered, there were also police officers present, and they mainly drove Volkswagen Golfs, [Interpreter's Note: "Type E," I believe the witness said]. Blue ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the Muslim refugees start arriving in Potocari from the direction of Srebrenica? Could you tell us the date, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: The refugees already had realised that the tension was mounting, so those refugees had been gathering a couple of days before the fall, they had been gathering around the compound. But to repeat, I don't know all the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President -- very well, then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness F, do you know where the transport of refugees from Potocari towards Bratunac by buses had begun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around noon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On what day, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Directly after the fall of the enclave, after the Serbs had entered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it on the day after the fall of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same day the enclave fell and the Serbs marched next to the compound, immediately vehicles were put on the disposal for the refugees, to take them away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the enclave fall on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, can we say that the evacuations started on the 12th -- I'm sorry, on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately after the Serbs had entered, the buses and trucks came to transport those people. They came immediately behind the troops. So it was prepared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this took place on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it on that day that you first saw General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next time you saw him was on the following day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him during two days; that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was on the following day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we say that you yourself concluded that, in addition to other officers, General Krstic was trying to look after the things, was trying to make sure that everything was going on according to a plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that was the case. Of course, I didn't know at that time what his function was. There were several officers present whom I didn't know. And it was their affair, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because such an operation is led on a high level, and that high level is usually present to see whether everything is going according to plan. Why else would they be there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after the second time you saw General Krstic, you never saw him again in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that a higher ranking officer of the VRS was arrested and that proceedings have been opened against him before this International Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that there were proceedings going on, but I never really followed against whom and why. I don't have time for that. I'm too busy with my work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A film was shown here in the Netherlands, whose authors, I believe, are some BBC journalists. The subject of the film were the events which took place in July 1995 in Srebrenica. The title of the film was "A Cry from the Grave" or "A Scream from the Grave." Have you seen that film, by any chance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, during five years, I only heard negative things about Srebrenica. That is why I did not -- I didn't want to deal with Srebrenica anymore. I had enough of it, like many of us. And I was not interested in Srebrenica anymore. I've been harassed by these events for long enough now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And lastly, Witness F, I should like to know whether, when you saw General Krstic, whether you also saw him giving any orders to his subordinates, to his subordinate officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I was not with the commanders, but if anything was discussed, it was said and it was talked about, and they made gestures and they moved their arms. But I don't know what was said. I don't understand the language. Of course, there were directions to follow plans. In the army, usually the case is that an order is given out, but it's never carried out as it was given, so you always have to adapt it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in this particular case, do you know which instructions we are talking about? I mean, the instructions emanating from General Krstic. And if you could please give me a yes or no to this question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was mainly about the transport being speeded up --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise, but I wanted a simple yes or no answer from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness F, you have been asked a question by Mr. Petrusic, who wanted to know whether you are able to -- that is, whether you were able to hear the instructions that were allegedly given by General Krstic to his subordinate officers, and I think that the answer should be yes or no. I hope I'm correctly interpreting your intervention, Mr. Petrusic. So, please, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the language, but orders were given.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have a bit of a contradictory answer here, because if you do not understand the language --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic -- sorry. I believe the witness has answered your question. Apparently, there is a slight contradiction, but the witness is a soldier and I believe that he's able to understand the so-called non-verbal aspects of the communication. He said that he did not hear the General give instructions because he doesn't speak the language, but it was his impression that he was giving instructions. So I think that we should accept this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I do not have any more questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, I did not want to interrupt the cross-examination, but I think that we should avoid repeating what was already said during the direct examination. We should have a very specific context, lay some foundations, and then ask specific questions. We, of course, have a possibility to discuss later on evidence given by witnesses in general. There will be enough time for that, and the Defence, as well as the Prosecution, will have an opportunity to do so at the end, to make their submissions. At this point in time, we are just hearing the evidence. You are doing your job, both the Defence and the Prosecution, and we, the Judges, are listening. So in future cases, please try not to oblige the witness to repeat what has already been said during the direct examination, and try to restrict yourself to specific and concrete questions. Thank you, once again, Mr. Petrusic. Mr. McCloskey, will there be any redirect examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just briefly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. McCloskey, let us hear you. Re-examined by Mr. McCloskey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you've testified that you're not sure about the various dates of these incidents; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you clear that the day that the Bosnian Serb troops came into Potocari is the same day that the transportation of the refugees began?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the Serbs had entered, immediately after them the vehicles arrived in order to transport the people. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't have anything further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. Judge Fouad Riad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I'll call you Witness F. Good morning. My questions will be of a general character and would help us draw the conclusions without going into details most of the time. In fact, my questions turn around to main things, the role of the Drina Corps in this organisation, which you mentioned was very well organised and it was a well-prepared stage. Now, what was the role of the Drina Corps, in your opinion, in this very well-organised stage? Was it a prominent role? Was it a leading role? What was your assessment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, to cleanse the area as quickly as possible, mop it up from all sides. As you know, there were also military advancing from Srebrenica. And from the vicinity of Bratunac, also units were advancing. So they closed the whole Muslim fighting area. That was a prepared operation, very well prepared indeed. And immediately afterwards, they mopped up the area, cleared it of all resistance, so that within a couple of days the area was under their command. So that the main road from Bratunac towards Srebrenica was in their own hands, because for them that was a main road in this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And the Drina Corps was there all the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was always present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Always present. And it is also a well-organised corps. What you said, that the Serbs were very well-organised, this applies also to the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And a good chain of command? I'm repeating you. With a good chain of command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, there was very good command. They were disciplined men, they were experienced military men. Indeed, it was a well-planned operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You did not notice that some soldiers were just going wild and doing whatever they wanted, killing or raping, whatever they wanted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the first stage, what I for myself -- what I called the disciplined military, had the main area to mop up the area as quickly as possible. And the second stage, those were the Rambo-types, a bit wild, indeed, who looted other houses, took away belongings, and I'm sure they have -- they committed -- the witnesses who committed human rights, they were under the command of another commanding person. I think they were kind of temporary soldiers, like temps. I don't think that the first line committed those acts, because they didn't have time for that. They had another duty. They had the duty to empty the area of rebels and resistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned several cases where you saw General Krstic. I noted them, but of course you know them as well as I. He was with General Mladic when he was distributing the sweets to the children, and then you saw him when he wanted to enter the compound to see how many refugees were there. That's the first day. You apparently saw him the second day, around the White House, looking whether everything went according to plan. And you also mentioned that you saw him with high-ranking officers of the VRS, standing and looking around to see if everything was according to plan, near the interrogation house. Apart from other things. And also you mentioned that he was there to see that everything was going according to plan. Now, doesn't that really -- that doesn't really fit in, when you say that the others were doing what they wanted. If he was there to see if everything was going to plan, then there was someone in control of the situation. Was he in control of the situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, he was constantly present, but those rebels or those Rambo-types just went their own way. On the second day, when I took the pictures in the vicinity, the pictures of the bodies, there were many Rambo-types around. They guarded the surroundings and they were in houses and on chairs, all sitting on material belonging to Muslims, and they used stuff and they took it along, and he didn't say anything about it. Those people carried alcohol, cigarettes. They had stolen our watches, our weapons, and nothing was said about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, to take an example, when you mentioned today that he was with high-ranking officers, standing and looking around, I even asked you what he was looking at. And the dead bodies which you spoke about, with the bloodstains on the back of their heads and so on, were lying behind -- were lying behind the interrogation house. Was it possible that he would just not see anything of what's happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nine to ten corpses which I found were diagonally in an open field at the edge of a forest, near a creek, behind the interrogation house, about 700 metres from the compound. I don't think it was visible by Dutch military men, but I'm sure that he knew about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: How far were these dead bodies from the interrogation house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: 400 to 450 metres. That's my estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And other things you mentioned, for instance, the babies -- when you mentioned the first night, people hanged themselves and there were dead babies inside the compound. Is anybody in control of this situation? Would it be possible for him to be completely unaware of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean somebody belonging to DutchBat?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: No. General Krstic. Somebody in control.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course they knew about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge Riad. I should like the witness to look again at Exhibit 5/2. Here it is. Witness F, you mentioned the site marked "F" as the point of observation where you observed a series of events which you then described to us; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you use the pointer and indicate on the ELMO -- will you please turn to the ELMO? Perhaps, Mr. Usher, you could help the witness. Can you tell us: What was the angle at which you were observing these events? Could you trace it? Could you mark it with the marker? Could you use the marker to show at which angle you were? Could you just draw at which angle were you watching it, the visual angle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to get our bearings right. Could you perhaps put next to letter "F", "north" and "south."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So now north is the direction of Bratunac. Is that so? And then Srebrenica to the south.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for west and east, we have mountains on those two sides.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I should like to ask you: How long were you at that particular site observing, more or less? How long did you observe them from that particular place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: The day before the fall, plus the night, till about 11.00 on the first day. I think 15 or 16 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if I understand you well, you were there on the 10th, during the night between the 10th and 11th, and on the 11th until about 11.00.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you go back to your observation point after 11.00 on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This position had been prepared when the situation -- when the tension was mounting, so it also had to be broken down. So this was an additional position on the compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you did not come back to this observation post. You picked out a different observation post; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. I had been assigned to another place, yes, and of course there was a command for me, when the Serbs had already entered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And where was this other observation post?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could you please ask the witness to start again. I'm sorry. Interpreter's mistake. Could you please ask the witness to start again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Excuse me, Witness F. You really have to speak slowly and make a pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And could the witness speak up, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need a double pause because we are not in the usual situation with the interpreters. With the working conditions that we have now, we need twice as much time for breaks so the interpreters can catch up with you. So will you please begin once again? So your second observation post, where was it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And could the witness speak up, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslim refugees were already present on the compound, and I was assigned to take up an additional position at the arrow "UN base." This was, at the same time, the toilet for all the Muslim refugees, so I was literally standing in you know what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My second question is as follows, Witness F: Where were you when you saw General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment -- at that moment, I was at the main entrance to the compound, this location [indicates].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another question. Where was General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the centre of all the happenings, around the refugees, so he was in the centre between the main entrance, the bus complex, and the White House, around the compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Witness F, I will ask you to use the pointer to show the place where you saw General Krstic. And I'm going to use also the transcript which the Prosecutor used -- I can use another letter, if we need one, in addition to the letter used by the Prosecutor. Can you show us on this exhibit, where were you when you saw General Krstic? Where was the place from which you saw General Krstic? And mark it with a "G". We had an "F" on the exhibit, didn't we?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very good. Now, will you mark the place where General Krstic was at the time, and put an "H" next to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another question, Witness F. How far away are points "H" and "G"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ten to fifteen metres. They just were walking around together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ten to fifteen metres; is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another question. Were there any barriers, anything that would obstruct your view, houses or trees or anything, between the place where you were standing and the place where General Krstic was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no obstacles, no trees, no rocks. There were security people, but nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So all the other VRS officers whom you mentioned, General Mladic, Commander Nikolic, and others, they were also there, at this place around point "H", were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around point "H".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another question. Why do you say that this person who is sitting behind in the dock is the same person that you saw from -- that you saw at point "H"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I see that you couldn't understand because I was trying not to lead you. You're saying that General Krstic, and that is the person who is sitting here in the bottom of this room, was on the 11th and the 12th of July -- that you saw him in that place. Why is it, how, on the basis of what are you concluding that this is one and the same person? Sorry. Did somebody tell you, "This is General Krstic," or did General Krstic meet you and introduce himself and say, "I'm General Krstic"? That is it. Can you understand now? How did you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody came up to me and told me that this is the General, but I recognise his face. I recognise it very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're saying that this is -- that this was General Krstic, because when you arrived here to the courtroom, you recognised this person as that person whom you already saw on the 11th and the 12th of July at that place. Is that what we can infer from your answer, Witness F?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Tell us another thing. On the 11th of July and on the 12th of July, so on the two occasions that you saw General Krstic, did you always see him at that same place, at "H", or did you see him in different places?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, he moved around, but I saw him at those points. And for the rest, I was busy with my own work. I didn't always pay attention to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, this was not my last question, Witness F. I'm sorry. I should like to -- if you can -- but I think that your training enables you to tell us the results of your observation. With regard to what you saw concerning General Krstic, what is it that you saw? Don't give us your conjectures, but if possible, describe to us -- because you had your camera. So as in a photograph, tell us, what did you observe with regard to General Krstic? It is both difficult and easy.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, it's difficult to find the right words to describe it. I think a mass murder of a great amount of people, of many people, which were taken out by military apparatus. And it was certainly well-prepared, and many civilians were victims of this, amongst them children, women, men, and that is to put it in very soft words. The film "Schindler's List" was nothing compared to that. It was really horrible. And you can understand that, for me, this is a very emotional affair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness F, I want to ask you now: General Krstic -- who did General Krstic talk to, if he talked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: With several officers. I apologise for being so emotional, but after five years, things are emerging.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is quite natural, Witness F. It is human to have emotions, and we understand how you feel and we respect that too. But if you answer my question, I will try to ask short questions, and you can answer them directly. If you want a break, then we can make a break. Shall we continue? Very well. Thank you. So were there some individuals who came and went to General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think they were mainly officers, and I didn't observe it for the rest. I was busy with other things, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And did General Krstic use some means of communication; that is, a radio, walkie-talkie, or something else that he used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't observe it directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From what you saw, were there some individuals who looked as if they were asking questions of General Krstic or supplying him with some information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. There was some consultation going on around the generals and the officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When General Krstic moved from the place where he spent most of the time, that is, point "H", and when he moved away from there, did you have an opportunity to see what he was going to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mainly he walked around and looked whether everything was going according to plan, but I didn't see what he did exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. I believe you have provided us with a great deal of information. I think that Judge Riad has yet another question. Judge Riad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Witness F, I'm not going to prolong your discomfort much longer, but to the best of your knowledge, and this is a question of general assessment and if you remember: Was General Krstic present all the time in all the events during these two days, or was he -- because you mentioned that he was there when they were distributing sweets to the children in front of the camera, and he was there to meet important people -- but apart from that, you never referred to him. You would say that General Krstic wanted to enter the compound to see how many refugees were hiding. It was Krstic that was entering, not Mladic. And in other cases, he was looking whether everything was according to plan. You referred to Krstic as if he was in control and there was no Mladic. Was Mladic not there anymore?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him anymore. I think he was one of the responsibles in assigning duties to the military.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So it appeared to you that it was Krstic who was in charge in the execution, and he had the control?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think he was one of the big officers who were in charge, yes, who had been assigned this task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Was it apparent that there was somebody higher than him, someone who Mladic considered higher in hierarchy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: No. My question is: Was there someone higher than Krstic in hierarchy, between Mladic Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that moment at that point and in that place, but I think there was some evaluation going on with the chief of staff in higher levels.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But not at this level, not on the ground.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not directly there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge Riad. Witness F, only a point of clarification. Exhibit 5/2, on which you marked the angles at which you observed, and for the record, can one say that basically your angle of observation was towards west or north, to the east, but not to the south? Yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. My view towards the south was blocked by the high tower on the compound. I could look over the roof of the compound till the high tower and the beginning of the compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I see. In any event, I believe the exhibit and the record show quite clearly that your field of visibility went in three directions, except for the south. Very well, Witness F. You have finished your testimony. You testified for a long time here. You lived through these events. The Prosecution, the Defence, and the Bench and the Chamber asked you a number of questions. But is there something that you would like to say and yet have had no opportunity to say before in answering questions? If there is anything of that kind, you can do so now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Again, for me, after five years, this is the first time I can talk about these photographs. Hardly anybody knew about it. I'm very grateful to you for listening to my story, and I think this is a very good thing for history and for human rights. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also hope, we all hope, Witness F, that it will also be good for you and for your peace of mind, having been able to say all those things, to recount all those things that you have kept to yourself for such a long time. We thank you very much for coming here. Somebody will help you leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before you release the witness, I am referring to 5/2A, as marked by the witness, 5/3A, 59, 60, 61, 62, and 63 are all Prosecution Exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We would tender those into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These exhibits were tendered and admitted. Mr. Dubuisson, you will take care of all the bureaucratic measures that are needed. Witness F, thank you. I should also like to thank the interpreters who were with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, before the break, what do we have next?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours; good morning, counsel. We have two witnesses remaining for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In open session or do we need any protection measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. Both witnesses will need protection measures. The first will be in public session with face distortion and a pseudonym; the second, we are requesting a closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, do you have any objection as to the application of protective measures? We know that in principle you do not object to protective measures, but it has to be made clear for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Before we began this morning, we didn't have an opportunity to consult, so I do not know the order of witnesses. So this should be perhaps left for after the break. We should be made familiar with the order of witnesses, because we do not know which particular witness is requesting what protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, can you respond to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I was under the impression that we did provide the order of witnesses, but if it's unclear, I'm happy to do so again over the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but as far as we understood you yesterday, there may have been some changes that occurred in the meantime. Mr. Harmon, is the order, therefore, the same as yesterday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that Mr. Harmon has suggested that you can solve the issue during the break. However, let me remind you of one thing that is quite important for our work, that is, how we should proceed, because during the break we can undertake all the necessary measures for the next witness. So Mr. Harmon said that he could tell you everything about the next witness during the break. Mr. Dubuisson, I hope that all the measures will be taken so that we can start right away with the witness once we come back from the break, and I hope that protective measures will be applied.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Very well, Mr. President. We will be sitting in public session for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. Can you hear me? Could you please now read the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated now. Are you comfortable, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope you have been well treated here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall try to do the same. Witness, I should like to thank you first for coming here, and let me just explain to you that you will first be answering questions put to you by Mr. Harmon, who is representing the Prosecution, as soon as we have made sure that everything is in order and that we can communicate properly. I can see that Mr. Harmon is satisfied that everything is okay. Mr. Harmon, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President, Judge Riad. Examined by Mr. Harmon:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you state your name?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Ademovic, Bego.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you spell your last name?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: A-d-e-m-o-v-i-c, "Bego" being my first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old are you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I didn't get a translation in the English.

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Fifty-eight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us; are you a Muslim by faith, Mr. Ademovic?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us about your education? How far did you go in school?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I have the first four forms of the elementary school, and I'm a driver by profession.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have some difficulty in reading?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't read very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were a driver by profession. How many years were you --

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- how many years were you a driver?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Thirty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of vehicles did you drive?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: All kinds of transport vehicles and buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where are were you employed as a driver?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I worked at the Vihor Company and the Partizanski Put Company in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is the Vihor Company located?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: In Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long were you employed as a driver in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I worked there for less than a year. I mean, I worked less than a year in the Partizanski Put Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, therefore, did you work for a number of years in Bratunac as a driver?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. I retired as a driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before the war started, where did you live?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: In the village of Dzile, the municipality of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are you married?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm a father of four children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to draw your attention to the events that took place before the fall of the Srebrenica enclave, and let me ask you; before the fall of the enclave, were you living in the village of Kutezero?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is that in relation to the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: It is situated in the direction of the Radava Mountain, in the vicinity of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far away is it from the town of Srebrenica, that particular village?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: About ten kilometres, I couldn't be more precise. Maybe less than ten kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were living in that village, with whom were you living?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: With my mother, with my uncle, my wife, my two sons, my two daughters-in-law, and my four grandchildren.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at some point in time, Mr. Ademovic, did the Bosnian Serb army come into the enclave and did you leave that village?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point in time, did you flee from the village of Kutezero?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I was living in Dzile, and then I fled Dzile after the fall of the Srebrenica municipality, and then I reached Kutezero. If you're asking me about the fall of Srebrenica, well, yes, at that time, I fled from Kutezero.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with whom did you flee the village?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I fled with my daughters-in-law, and with my mother, and my uncle had died before the fall of Srebrenica, and our grandchildren were with us as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you flee?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I fled from Chetniks. I didn't want to be slaughtered by them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: We went to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did all of you who had fled from your village arrive in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your mother arrive in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: My mother couldn't walk, so she couldn't continue, and she remained in the woods, and that's where she died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you; do you remember the day when you arrived in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: It was on a Tuesday, on the 11th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the 11th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you and your wife and other members of your family take refuge?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: At the Zinc Factory in Potocari. There were lots of people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived in the Zinc Factory, was there any shooting going on in and around the Zinc Factory?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: There was some shelling and some gunfire. People got injured by shells, fragments of shells. There may have been casualties or fatalities, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you arrived in Potocari on the 11th of July, were there other refugees in and around the Zinc Factory?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, a lot of people, a crowd of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to estimate how many people there were?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Over 2.000 or 3.000, probably more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and your wife and family members take refuge inside the Zinc Factory or outside on the grounds around the Zinc Factory?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Around the Zinc Factory, coming from the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at some point in time, did members of the Bosnian Serb army arrive in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did members of the Bosnian Serb army arrive in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: On the following day, after 10.00, on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that would be the 12th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you see in which direction the Bosnian Serb soldiers were coming?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: We were first told to clear the asphalt area, that soldiers would be coming from the direction of Srebrenica, and they came in in a column of two, and then they continued towards Bratunac. And then Chetniks started arriving from all directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you recognise any members of the Bosnian Serb army who had come in to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I recognised only a colleague of mine from Vihor, Lazic. He worked there as a bus driver, and he was working in the reserve section.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "the reserve section," do you mean the reserve section of the bus company or the reserve section of the army?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Of the former Yugoslavia, Tito's Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "reserve section," what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, he was wearing clothes, this particular suit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the particular suit he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: It was grey in colour. It was a warm kind of clothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see anybody else?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't recognise anyone else. I didn't recognise anyone in the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, later on, notice any Bosnian Serb soldiers you knew by name who may not have walked in in the column but may have been walking amongst the people?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: There was a huge crowd of people, and I knew only knew Zoran Mirosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: He was wearing a camouflage suit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you to focus your attention on that day again, the 12th of July, and ask you if you saw a conversation taking place between a Bosnian Serb soldier and a family of Bosnian Muslims. Did you see a conversation taking place, and could you describe to the Judges what you saw and what you heard?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were lots of Chetniks walking around, quite a few people were sitting next to me. There was one man, together with his wife and their two children, son and daughter. Two soldiers approached them. They said hello to the man and the girl, and they inquired about their health. And they said to the man, "Let us take your wife and your daughter so that they can be put on the first buses," and the man said, "No. We're not going to separate." But they grabbed the girl and they took her away from him. The wife fainted, and the man was motionless. He was simply watching this thing happen. And the girl was taken away in the direction of Srebrenica, from the Zinc Factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to that girl?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges how those soldiers were dressed?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage suits.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour was the camouflage?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: It was multi-coloured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any particular dominant colour, any particular ...

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't very visible. I'm not a specialist for colours. It was difficult to tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know the kind of camouflage uniforms worn by the army and the kind of camouflage uniforms worn by the police? Do you know the difference between those two?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. I cannot tell the difference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the names of those particular soldiers who took away the girl?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know them at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while you were in the Zinc compound area, did you see other Serb soldiers walking among the refugees?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see them do anything. They were just cursing at people, calling them names, telling them that they would be slaughtered, that they would end out their lives there. They were telling them to leave the area, that it was a Serb country, that it was part of the Greater Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how were the soldiers who were making those curses, do you remember how they were dressed?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: The same. The same kind of suit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Camouflage suits; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Camouflage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see any particular marks or badges or patches on those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I could only see them on Zoran Mirosavljevic, but those who were cursing did not wear any insignia. Only Zoran had some kind of badge on his arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what kind of badge Zoran had on his arm? Could you describe it?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot describe it. I only saw that he had some kind of insignia, but I wasn't paying attention to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ademovic, at some point in time when you were walking in and around the Zinc Factory, did you see a violent incident involving a child?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges what you saw?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, tell the Judges what you saw.

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: After they'd taken away the girl, the situation was a bit calmer. I walked around the Zinc Factory -- I wanted to get to my wife and my daughter-in-law -- and I went by a soldier where there was many people. There was a woman carrying a child in her arms, and the soldier asked her whether the baby's name was Alija. She said it wasn't. Then he inquired whether it was a boy, and the woman said yes. Then he bent down, took a knife out, he took the baby and hit the baby with a knife here, like this. I turned around and the baby fell down. It was dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "he hit the baby here," where did he strike the baby with the knife?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Here [indicates], in the chest. Under the head, near the neck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I went back. I didn't know what happened then. I only learned that the child was dead. But I fled in the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell the Judges how that soldier was dressed?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: He had the same kind of suit as others were wearing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is a camouflage suit.

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, camouflage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that that baby was murdered, were there other refugees in and around that crime scene?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You couldn't move through them. They were standing next to each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reaction of the people who saw this killing of this child?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: There wasn't much reaction. After that, it was as if things were normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And later on in the day -- let me ask you this question, Mr. Ademovic: About what time of the day did that happen, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't have a watch, but I think that it could have been around 12.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you, that day, attempt to go get some water for your family?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I went up the hill, in the direction of Srebrenica, and wanted to take some water. I also wanted to get some food. I wanted to find something to cook for my children. And then I was stopped by a soldier. And this took place before 10.00. There were Serb troops over there, and there was a kind of ribbon which prevented us from moving on. So I turned around and went back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I went outside the compound of the Zinc Factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where outside the compound of the Zinc Factory did you go?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Outside the Zinc Factory. I mean, up the hill, towards a barn. There were a lot of people there. The situation was somewhat calmer at that point in time, and people were moving around. They went up to a meadow, and they were drinking and eating, but they were mostly silent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you with anybody?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: I was with Dzemal Karic. There were a lot of people around us, but the two of us stuck together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point in time, did a Serb soldier appear?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they appeared from behind. We spent some time sitting there, and at one point somebody said that Serb soldiers were coming. And people fled to the Zinc Factory. And the two of us, we went to a barn and we hid there. And we didn't follow the people who went towards the Zinc Factory, and they didn't see us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were hidden in a barn or near a barn, on a hillside, overlooking the Zinc Factory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: There was a shed below the stable, and we hid behind that shed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see when you hid behind that shed?

utterances.speaker: BEGO ADEMOVIC
utterances.text: Two Serb soldiers followed the people, and they went in through a hole of the Zinc Factory fence. They took three Bosniak men from that -- through that hole, and they moved in the direction of Aljo's house. We saw them, and we were actually watching in their direction. There were between 10 and 15 people there, between the Zinc Factory and Aljo's house. There was a kind of ramp that had been prepared there, and they moved the people towards that location. There were two Chetniks and some other soldiers as well, and they were taking people -- taking men by their arms. They would hold them by an arm behind their back.
